summary: The charter of the ARPANET Users Interest Working Group, called USING, formed at a May 1973 meeting of 15 network people to improve the network user's working environment. It sets out the group's background and aim of representing user needs.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 584 sets out the purpose, membership and goals of USING, a group formed to represent ARPANET users' needs. It describes short-term plans for user tools and guidance, along with longer-term ways to gather feedback and support new users.

subtitle: The charter for a group that represented ARPANET user interests.

tldr.problem: The charter says the ARPANET needed to better understand user needs as it developed into a service.
tldr.mechanism: The Users Interest Working Group, USING, would represent user interests and forward ideas from the broader USERS forum to relevant centers.
tldr.outcome: The charter sets near-term objectives such as a common command language and a new-users handbook, plus longer-term user-support activities.

today: RFC 584 is the charter for the ARPANET Users Interest Working Group and records its stated goals and planned activities.

sections.title: USING and the USERS Forum
sections.content: The ARPANET Users Interest Working Group, identified as USING, formed after a meeting of network people on May 23, 1973. Its aim was to represent the interests and needs of the network community and encourage better provision of services. A separate group, USERS, provided a forum for interested people to express requests and complaints; USING acted as its steering committee and passed ideas to the appropriate centers.
sections.plainLanguage: USING was meant to bring user needs to the people responsible for network services. The broader USERS group gave interested people a place to share requests and complaints.

sections.title: Membership and User Support
sections.content:
Membership in USING was open to people interested in improving network user support who were willing and able to contribute. Membership in USERS was open to any interested person. USING focused on network activities affecting services, including resource availability, reliability and ease of use.

The charter's overall goal was a coherent network environment that let users choose how much system detail and assistance they wanted. It called for self-documenting resources and assistance both online and offline.
sections.plainLanguage: USING expected its members to contribute work, while anyone interested could join USERS. Its scope covered whether network resources were available, reliable and easy to use.

sections.title: Objectives and Longer-Term Work
sections.content: For its initial 6–12 months, USING listed five objectives: specify a user-level Common Command Language, specify a network editor for that language, focus user issues, encourage a user consulting service and publish a new-users handbook. Longer-term activities included supporting directories, tutorials and training; creating ways to collect and respond to feedback; describing user requirements; helping new users join; and sponsoring seminars and working groups.
sections.plainLanguage: The group planned common user tools and a handbook first. Longer term, it aimed to improve training, feedback, access for new users and discussion among users.
